## Estimators

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_N$ be i.i.d. with $\mathbb{E}[X_i] = \mu$ and $\operatorname{Var}(X_i) = \sigma^2 < \infty$. The sample mean $\hat\mu_N = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N X_i$ has $\mathbb{E}[\hat\mu_N] = \mu$ and standard error $\sigma/\sqrt{N}$, so $\hat\mu_N \to \mu$ as $N \to \infty$. For a function $g$ with $g'(\mu) \neq 0$, the delta method gives $\operatorname{Var}(g(\hat\mu_N)) \approx g'(\mu)^2 \sigma^2 / N$, and the bias of $g(\hat\mu_N)$ is of order $1/N$ when $g''$ is bounded on $[\mu - \varepsilon, \mu + \varepsilon]$.

::: {#thm-clt}
## Central limit theorem
With $\sigma^2 = \operatorname{Var}(X_1) < \infty$, $\sqrt{N}\,(\hat\mu_N - \mu) / \sigma$ converges in distribution to $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Expand the characteristic function $\varphi(t) = \mathbb{E}[e^{itX}]$ to second order about $t = 0$.
:::

A paragraph between blocks, with $p_i = P(X = x_i)$ and $\sum_i p_i = 1$ inline.

::: {.callout-important}
## The $N^{-1/2}$ rate
The standard error of an average of $N$ i.i.d. samples falls like $N^{-1/2}$, whatever the problem.
:::

- A first item that runs long enough to wrap onto a second line, with $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f_X(x)\,dx = 1$ in it.
- A second item with $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}_A] = P(A)$.

### Confidence intervals

::: {#def-ci}
## Confidence interval
A $1 - \alpha$ confidence interval for $\theta$ is $\hat\theta_N \pm z_{\alpha/2}\,\widehat{\operatorname{SE}}$.
:::

| Level | $z_{\alpha/2}$ | Width in standard errors of the estimate |
|-------|----------------|------------------------------------------|
| 68%   | 1.00           | about two, one on each side of the estimate |
| 95%   | 1.96           | about four, which most reports quote |

::: {#exr-ci}
## Coverage
Draw $N = 100$ samples many times and count how often the interval covers $\mu$.
:::

A closing paragraph.
